dynamic_evidence: r64 exposed equal-count candidate rejection followed by owner drift.
A pytest PDB run disproved the first overly broad test: an ordinary equal-count verifier outcome without a candidate transaction must not emit candidate-rejection ownership.

r66 live same-run QA recovery kept all three rejected attempts on src/inkwell/cipher.cpp; every candidate guard restored bytes and no attempt drifted to cli_main.cpp or diary.cpp.
The existing three-nonprogress hard fuse still terminated the loop.
root_cause: candidate_rejection_target_files_for_next_round was emitted only for selected verifier-effect classes instead of for every candidate_rejected transaction. Restoration makes every rejected candidate non-authoritative regardless of whether the verifier classified it as regression, equal-count swap, or stagnant.

fix.invariant: Every candidate_rejected round preserves the exact normalized repair_target_files for the next same-diagnostic retry; accepted candidates do not gain this projection.
